We can adopt CareUI fully. **`@base-ui/react` would still be required**, because CareUI itself builds on it—its [Button component imports Base UI directly](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/careui/blob/main/src/components/ui/button.tsx).

The current implementation is partial:

- It includes 12 CareUI components, including Button, Input, Field, Tabs, and Table.
- CareUI’s theme is scoped to preserve the existing application’s styling.
- Referral screens still use existing Radix-based dialogs, selects, and popovers.

CareUI currently distributes components through a [shadcn registry](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/careui/blob/main/REGISTRY.md); its repository is marked private in [package.json](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/careui/blob/main/package.json). So adoption means installing its component source and theme, rather than adding a single `careui` package import.

**I recommend completing CareUI adoption across the referral flow**, including the remaining dialogs and selectors. The partial integration leaves us maintaining two component styles within the same feature. Replacing the shared components throughout CARE would be a broader migration; merely importing the entire registry wouldn’t update their existing usages.
